261:
Cerdeña, Mangubat, Gelisan, and Crisanto investigated quality assurance in the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) MOOC "Principles of Graphic Design." Using Biggs’ 3P Model, the researchers focused on the "product" variable to assess learning outcomes. The methodology combined Learning Management System (LMS) analytics with a Qualtrics survey based on the Commonwealth of Learning’s guidelines. The study analyzed a sample of 7,239 learners from an initial enrollment of 22,942 students.

The findings revealed high success across measured variables. The course achieved a 33.21% completion rate, with 7,620 students receiving certificates. Learner enjoyment was overwhelmingly positive regarding outcomes perception, continuing education, and employment opportunities, all scoring above 4.0. The socializing dimension was the only area receiving a neutral rating. Regarding self-satisfaction, 77.95% of respondents reported being "very satisfied," with the highest ratings attributed to course materials, followed by the teacher/coordinator, assessment, and learner support. Qualitative feedback described materials as "helpful" and "useful," and instructors as "informative."

The study concludes the MOOC is highly effective in terms of enjoyment, satisfaction, and completion. Results suggest learners prioritize practical knowledge over social interaction. Researchers suggest improving the socializing component through collaborative activities to foster 21st-century skills. This study provides a validated methodology for post-delivery evaluation and suggests future research into the relationship between enrollment intentions and completion rates.
